findings.detail: The Recommendations say what to do but do not explain why, although the specification requires a rationale. The historical GIA value also adds unnecessary detail to a section meant to remain high-level.
report_quote: We agreed to disinvest the joint GIA in full.
We recommend using the gross proceeds of c. £45,000 to top up David’s and Susan’s Stocks & Shares ISAs for the new tax year, split equally between the two ISAs.
Your joint General Investment Account was previously shown in our records (15 March) as £40,000.

findings.detail: This presents the full gross proceeds as going into the ISAs. The meeting note says both ISAs are already part-funded and the top-up must use their remaining allowances, so the report states the allocation more definitively than the source permits. The later adviser marker does not qualify this recommendation.
report_quote: We recommend using the gross proceeds of c. £45,000 to top up David’s and Susan’s Stocks & Shares ISAs for the new tax year, split equally between the two ISAs.

findings.detail: The report does not leak the internal notes, but only dates the older GIA figure. It does not identify when the approximate current value was observed, making it harder to distinguish the live meeting figure from account valuations recorded at other times. This is a minor lapse in following the instruction to attend to figure dates.
report_quote: | H-GIA-J | David Clarke & Susan Clarke | General Investment Account | c. £45,000 |
Your joint General Investment Account was previously shown in our records (15 March) as £40,000.

findings.detail: The report switches between describing David and Susan as third-party clients and addressing them directly. It also uses ‘CGT’ before explaining the abbreviation. Both are minor obstacles to an otherwise readable report.
report_quote: Both clients are now retired and confirmed that their objectives and circumstances remain unchanged since the last review.
This figure is gross before any CGT and becomes available once the disposal completes.

findings.detail: All four markers identify the specific charge, tax question or ISA allocation to confirm and name the relevant platform or accounts.
